newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italy mkts wave aside report of EMU entry delay.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italy mkts wave aside report of EMU entry delay.

text.p: Italian financial markets waved aside a report on Wednesday that there was a European plan afoot to delay Italy's entry to a single currency.

Traders said the report came as no surprise but for now, with official denials from Brussels, Bonn and Rome of any deal in the offing, markets were willing to believe the timing of Italy's entry into economic and monetary union (EMU) remained open.
"The markets are giving trust to the situation as it stands," one bond futures broker in London said.
A Financial Times report said Italy would be offered a deal to delay EMU entry until 2000 or 2001 instead of the projected 1999 debut, an idea denied by governments across Europe.
The denials undermined dealers' belief that any plan, if it existed, was far advanced and brokers said rejection of the idea by Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi boosted bonds.
But the report wrenched back into focus Italy's borderline status as a potential first-tier member of EMU.
"Most houses didn't think Italy would be ready for 1999 and that it might have to seek some sort of compromise parameters," said Luca Jellinek, bond strategist at Paribas Capital Markets.
The prospect of delay with a definite chance of entry later would not necessarily be that negative in the long term, Jellinek said.

A lira dealer at an Italian bank in London thought a delay of a year or two was not a major problem, saying: "Personally I think in the long run delay isn't necessarily a bad thing if it's going to create stability in the future."
Italian government bond (BTP) futures fell at the start as players sold on the FT report but then rallied 70 basis points as arbitrage trade between cash and futures drove them higher.
The lira tripped, dipping past its central parity of 990 against the mark in the exchange rate mechanism (ERM), but then climbed back to 984.50 by 1400 GMT as dollar strength aided it.
The Milan stock market calmly gained around 1.2 percent with the blue-chip Mib30 index at 18,671.

Markets were also cheered by a wage deal between Italian engineering unions and their employers after months of acrimonious dispute and by the apparent willingness of opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi to discuss a government proposal to bring forward the 1998 budget.
Dealers said in bonds there had been strong domestic buying on a low inflation and interest rate outlook for Italy.

Optimism has built up recently that Italy, which is striving hard to meet EMU convergence criteria, might squeeze in at the new currency's start, leading investors to buy into BTPs on the back of its economic efforts.
The FT report initially deflated that optimism. It was a reminder of ordinary Germans' worry over a single currency which might include Italy as they await elections next year.
Some analysts said a market peril now would be official confirmation that Italy would be asked to delay, or a political squabble over EMU which would harm the government's credibility.

Francesco Giordano, senior economist at San Paolo bank, doubted a compromise existed which would satisfy Italy, given the economic efforts it was making and its ever increasing chances of meeting some of the EMU criteria.
"It would be very difficult for anyone to keep Italy out if it reaches three or four of the five criteria," Giordano said.
"The risk is more to general EMU - that the Germans say 'OK with Italy in we'll postpone the whole thing by two years'."
